items.text: Figure 2.11Forces can cause changes in shape.

items.label: text
items.text: Wehave seen thatforcescan make thingsstart tomove,accelerate or decelerate.The examplesinFigure 2.11show anothereffect that forces can have-they can change the shapeofan object.

items.label: text
items.text: Sometimes the change of shape is temporary,as in the suspension spring in the mountain bike（Figure2.11a).Sometimes the shapeof theobjectis permanently changed,like a crushed can ora car that has collidedwith a load.Next we willlook at temporary changes in the lengths of springs and elasticbands.

items.label: text
items.text: Ifyouapply a force toan elasticband,itsshape changes-theband stretches andgets longer.All materialswill stretch a littlewhenyouput themunder tension (that is,pull them)or shorten whenyou compress or squash them.You can stretch a rubberband quite easily,but a huge force isneeded to cause a noticeable extension in a pieceof steel of the same length.

items.label: text
items.text: Some materials,like glass,donot change shape easily and arebrittle,breaking rather than stretchingnoticeably.Elasticmaterialsdonotbreakeasily and tend toretum totheiroriginalshapewhentheforcesactingon themareremoved. like the spring inFigure 2.11b.Othermaterials,likeputty and modelling clay arenotelastic butplastic,and they change shape when even quite small forcesare applied to them.

items.label: text
items.text: We will lookatelasticmaterials,likerubber,metal wires and metals formed intosprings,in thenext part of this chapter.

items.label: text
items.text: Springs are coiled lengths of certain types of metal,which can be stretched situations.Sometimes they are used toabsorbraised bumps in the road as suspension springsin a carorbicycle.Inbeds and chairs theyareused to make sleeping and sittingmore comfortable.Theyare alsoused in doorlocks tohold them closed and to make doors close automatically.

items.label: text
items.text: Robert Hooke discovered anotherimportantproperty of springs.He used simple apparatuslike that shown inFigure2.12.

items.label: text
items.text: Hooke measured the increasein length(extension)produced by different load forces on springs.The graphhe obtained byplotting force againstextension was a straight line passing through theorigin.This showsthat the extensionof the spring isproportional to the force.Thisrelationship is known as Hooke's law.
